title: RawStepMap
description: A step map as it is written, before anything has checked what it claims.

format.description: The format version the document says it is written in.

id.description: What this map is, such as `development/default`.

states.description: What to do in each state, by state name.

title.description: A human sentence for a report's heading.

workflow.description:
The workflow it is written against, pinned to a major version.

Read as a [`WorkflowRef`] so an unpinned one reaches validation and is refused there, **accumulating** with every other problem in the document rather than short-circuiting as a deserialization error would. The published schema is [`PinnedWorkflowRef`]'s, which is the strict one — the two halves of review finding F6.

EvidenceKind.description: A kind of evidence. The canonical names come first; the rest are older spellings still accepted.

Expect.description:
Which exit status of a `command` step is the passing verdict.

`failure` is how a bug fix names its reproducing command: the command is expected to fail before the fix, so a nonzero exit is what *reproduced* means, and an exit of zero is a failing verdict whose reason is [`NOTHING_REPRODUCED`]. A process that did not finish is still no verdict at all, whatever the step expects.

oneOf.description: Exit `0` is the pass, as every step before the key existed read it.
Any exit but `0` is the pass; exit `0` reproduced nothing.

PinnedWorkflowRef.description: Reference to a workflow at a major version, such as `adp/default/1`. The version is mandatory: a step map is an instruction sheet for one state graph.

RawEvidenceMapping.description: How a command's result becomes evidence, as written.

kind.description: Which kind of evidence the program establishes.

record.description: Where the program writes the evidence record, when it writes one itself.

tool.description: The tool that produced it, for provenance.

verifier.description: Which class of verifier it is.

RawScopeRule.description: One rule of a step's write scope, as written.

paths.description: The paths this rule is about, as globs relative to the working tree.

write.description: What writing is allowed on them.

concurrent.description:
Whether the state's consecutive `command` steps run at once.

Each maximal run of consecutive `command` steps is then one batch: its steps run at once, and their results are submitted in map order once every one of them has ended. An `llm` or `operator` step is a barrier between batches. Absent is `false`: one step at a time.

steps.description: The steps, in the order the author wants them run.

visit_budget.description: How many times this state may be entered before the run stops.

oneOf.description: Run a program and map its result to evidence.

circuit_breaker.description: After how many failures of `depends_on` to stop attempting it in this run.

depends_on.description: The outside thing this step needs, if it needs one.

description.description: What this step is for, in one line.

evidence.description: What to record when the program produces a verdict.

expect.description: Which exit status is the passing verdict. `success` when the document is silent.

output.description: A file name in the run directory the program's standard output is written to.

retries.description: How many times to retry a step that could not run at all.

oneOf.description: Ask a model, with a tool set the protocol derived.

commands.description:
The commands this step's shell admits, each an argv prefix with the program first.

`[[aep, plan, artifact]]` admits one simple invocation of `aep plan artifact …` and nothing else; `[[task], [cargo, test]]` admits the repository's tasks and `cargo test`. Absent means the step declares nothing and is held to the driver's default surface.

context.description:
Files the run is given before it starts, instead of discovering them.

A list and never a glob: a glob is a promise about a directory's future size, and a step map is pinned. A named file that is absent at run time refuses the run — a run given a smaller context than its map declares is one nobody can reproduce from the map.

Not free. A stateless harness replays its conversation every turn, so a preloaded file is paid for on every turn rather than once. It is still usually a saving, because what it replaces — a discovery read — is a call, a turn, *and* a result that joins the same replay.

description.description: What this step is for, in one line.

harness.description: Which harness runs it. `claude-code` when the document is silent.

judgement.description:
What this step decides that no command could, in one line.

Required in an `aep.driver-steps/2` map and optional in an `aep.driver-steps/1` one, so it is read as optional: a `/2` step without one reaches validation and is refused there with its path, accumulating with every other problem in the map, rather than failing the whole document as a deserialization error would. The published schema requires it for `/2` at the map's level, where the format version is.

prompt.description: What the model is asked to do.

scope.description: Where this step may write, in order. First match wins.

skills.description: Skills the harness should make available, by name.

oneOf.description: Stop and hand the run to a person.

description.description: What this step is for, in one line.

prompt.description: What the person is being asked for.

StepMapId.description: Identifier of a step map, such as `development/default`.

TestSuite.description: Which body of tests was run.

Verifier.description: A verifier class; the named classes are listed in `examples`, and any other name is treated as an external tool.

WriteScope.description:
How much of a file an operation class may change, where a scope rule admits it at all.

**Granularity, not identity.** A step map is a document about work; naming an operation here — `file.write`, `file.edit` — would couple it to another protocol's vocabulary at its most volatile point, and every operation added later would need a key in every map or silently fall outside every scope. Which of a harness's operations replace a whole file is that harness's fact, and it is the one place that knows.

Three words, and `PartialOnly` is not invented for the planning store: it is a property the tool catalogues already document — *write one file, whole* against *change part of one*.

oneOf.description: Anything in the class may act on these paths.
Part of a file may be changed; a whole file may never be replaced.
Nothing in the class may act here.
